questions.solution_en:
Option a) is correct because "committee" is a singular collective noun, and the singular verb "has" agrees with it.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

Option b) is incorrect because "have" is used for plural subjects, and "committee" is singular.

Option c) is incorrect because "is decided" is grammatically incorrect; it should be "has decided." "Is decided" is the passive voice construction which does not fit in this sentence as the emphasis is on the doer of the action, the committee.

Example:

Active- Radha will work. (emphasis on Radha)

Passive- Work will be done by Radha. (emphasis on Work)

Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I need to buy a pair of pants that are blue in colour for our upcoming drama at school.
questions.q_hi:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I need to buy a pair of pants that are blue in colour for our upcoming drama at school.
options_en: I need to buy a pair
options_hi: I need to buy a pair
questions.solution_en:
The error lies in option (c).

'Pants' exist in plural form only. But, when it is expressed in the singular form, it is written as 'a pair of pants' ('pair' becomes the subject). As it is singular in form, the verb that follows it must also be singular.

For example: A pair of pants is kept inside the almirah.

Similarly, in this question, a singular verb must agree with 'a pair of pants'. So, 'is' must replace 'are' in the sentence.

Thus, the error is in option (c).

Therefore, the corrected form of the sentence is: I need to buy a pair of pants that is blue in colour for our upcoming drama at school.

Additional Information:

Certain nouns like this exist in plural form only. Thus, they take a plural verb.
